body: The `initialUiState` is only provided on the first search. Dynamically added widgets ignore the option.

```suggestion
   * Injects a `uiState` to the `instantsearch` instance. You can use this option
```
By this you mean that it's only used by the `init` of the index itself, right?
was thinking on allowing the string `instant_search` specifically, or else we can do it with indexId, but also fine to just ignore here
would  be nice if we could avoid storing it, but since we need it in `start`, not in the constructor, it isn't possible

I mean, only on the first loop over the `init` lifecycle. A widget (it includes `index`) dynamically added won't take into account the `initialUiState`. It's the same behaviour with the `searchParameters`.
Not sure it's really useful, until now we don't have it that much inside the codebase.
Can we make this test name clearer? Do you mean "forwards the init `uiState` to the widget state"?
We don't test for nested indices?

No we don't, it's already covered inside [`index`](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/271fc7b2cd905d3ca388a5e31ecd2b4c2e3ca27e/src/widgets/index/__tests__/index-test.ts#L1379-L1435). From the InstantSearch perspective it's the same, it doesn't matter if there is 1 or 100 indices.

```
uses the provided `uiState` for the local `uiState`
```

Is it better?
